profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap point, tagged telecom=data_center, is named "Factory Software | AVEVA Select Italia." AVEVA is a real, publicly traded industrial software company, listed on the London Stock Exchange, that provides engineering design, operations management, and asset-performance software used across manufacturing, energy, and process industries worldwide. "AVEVA Select" is the branding AVEVA uses for its network of regional reseller and systems-integrator partners, and this record most plausibly identifies an Italian partner office selling and supporting AVEVA's software products under that program, likely operating under the name "Factory Software" as the local reseller entity. A software reseller and integrator's office maintains its own business IT systems but is not a data-center operator; the telecom=data_center tag here is best read as a mistag of the office's own server or IT closet.

reading.body:
This record is a software reseller's office, not a data center, and its zero megawatts reflect that.

The point carries an OpenStreetMap tag of telecom=data_center, but the name resolves to an Italian partner office of AVEVA, an industrial software vendor. A reseller and systems integrator runs business IT and perhaps a server closet. That is not a facility with a power contract, a cooling plant, or a grid interconnection.

The distinction matters because data-center counts assembled from volunteered geographic data will absorb these mistags. A single office contributes no load, yet it enters the same category as buildings that draw tens or hundreds of megawatts. Any tally of Italian data-center capacity built from this source alone would overstate the number of sites and say nothing reliable about megawatts.

What the data does not cover is the actual data-center capacity of Italy. It gives one point, at coordinates near Milan Malpensa airport, with no operator, no website, and no built date. The megawatt figure of zero is a default for a non-facility, not a measurement.
